physical_harm: The victim suffered bum injuries leading to her death
number_of_offences: Convicted under one count, upheld by the court
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the dying declaration of the victim, which stated that her mother-in-law (the appellant) sprinkled kerosene oil on her and burnt her, and also noted the trial court's application of Section 113-B of the Evidence Act.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the victim's dying declaration as veracious and did not doubt its truth, as she did not make any allegations against her sister-in-law who was also present.
post_offence_conduct: The appellant has already served 14 years and 6 months of imprisonment in jail, and the court requested the authorities to consider her case for premature release strictly in accordance with law.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 25.6.1999, Trial judgment: 15.12.2000, High Court decision: 13.04.2007, Supreme Court decision: 17.04.2013
legal_representation: Manoj Prasad, S.S. Gupta for the Appellant; Ravi Prakash Mehrotra, Ram Kishor Singh Yadav for the Respondent
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction under Section 302, High Court: Affirmed conviction, Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant poured kerosene oil on her daughter-in-law and set her on fire, leading to her death. The dying declaration of the victim, recorded by the magistrate, was used to establish the guilt of the appellant.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellant had already served 14 years and 6 months of imprisonment and that her case for premature release under Section 432 CrPC had not been considered by the State.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the presumption under Section 113-B of the Evidence Act, which presumes that a dowry demand was made in cases of cruelty leading to death.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence of life imprisonment was imposed based on the victim's dying declaration and the presumption under Section 113-B of the Evidence Act, which established the guilt of the appellant.
other_sentence_order: The court requested the authorities to consider the appellant's case for premature release under Section 432 CrPC strictly in accordance with the law.
